claims.text: The proposed hybrid model will predict Young’s modulus within ±5% of experiment.
The proposed hybrid model will predict yield strength within ±5% of experiment.
The proposed hybrid model will predict toughness within ±5% of experiment.
The proposed pipeline will reduce computational cost by approximately 80% relative to conventional CALPHAD and first-principles approaches.
Multilevel chemical fluctuations mediate localized stress responses in the alloy.
The hierarchical microstructure mediates crack propagation.
Simulation-derived microstructural descriptors encode the effects of chemical fluctuations and hierarchical structure on stress response and crack propagation.
Combining reduced-order simulation descriptors with machine-learning feature selection captures complex nonlinear relationships between microstructure and mechanical behavior.
The proposed approach can bypass much of the computational intensity of traditional thermophysical calculations.
Standard CALPHAD, first-principles, and traditional machine-learning methods require extensive computational resources.
Existing computational methods have limited predictive accuracy for toughness.
Model reliability will decrease for conditions not represented in the training data.
Extreme temperatures or high strain rates will reduce the reliability of the model when those regimes are absent from training.
Synthesis defects that alter the hierarchical structure beyond the modeled range will reduce prediction reliability.

contradictions.description: The claimed accuracy is conditioned on adequate training-set representation and reliability is explicitly expected to decrease out of distribution, yet the benchmark includes out-of-training-distribution samples and falsifies the entire hypothesis if any property for any such sample exceeds 5% error. Thus the falsification rule tests outside the stated domain of reliability.
